findings.summary: Successful existing-connection update branch unverified
findings.evidence: Pre-verified gap: create-only successes and stale-update rejection never executed the update branch. New actual HTTP success asserts retained ID, changed persisted fields, unchanged count and authoritative result.

findings.summary: Late Connect effects discarded
findings.evidence: Initial onSuccess returned before any authoritative refresh when current(intent) failed. Fresh origin-scoped recovery now refreshes connection/safety/credential queries and retains scoped file-effect notices without replacing drafts; late-result and Restore consumer tests pass.

findings.summary: Lost Connect response permits duplicate creation
findings.evidence: Initial transport failure only advised Verify again after a possible commit. Explicit saved-state review now blocks retry, refreshes authoritative data and reuses an unambiguous existing ID; lost-response and failed-recovery tests pass.

findings.summary: Shared credential file has only Project admission
findings.evidence: Two Projects could interleave rename and status awaits before either transaction. Shared token-finalization admission now refuses the second call and releases on every exit; controlled cross-Project and failure retry cases pass.

findings.summary: CLI fingerprint checked before later status await
findings.evidence: The later credential-status probe could observe an altered CLI identity. Final operational resolution and private source/hash comparison now occur after that await and immediately before UoW; controlled account/removal tests pass.

findings.summary: Token proof omits reviewed operational CLI identity
findings.evidence: Verify displayed a source but retained only candidate token hash. Proof now privately binds reviewed operational source/hash and refuses CLI installation/removal/account drift after file storage with truthful retained-file effects.

findings.summary: Reconnect ignores selected connection
findings.evidence: The panel omitted connection prop. It now passes the selected configuration and distinguishes uninitialized selection from explicit New; HTTP stable-ID and consumer selection tests pass.

findings.summary: Malformed nonblank inputs become generic request errors
findings.evidence: Nonblank admission allowed malformed owner/repo/token to HTTP. Shared candidate schema now rejects them locally with actionable central text before mutation; invalid-input and cache privacy tests pass.

findings.summary: Failed safety read silently blocks Verify
findings.evidence: canVerify required safety.data but surfaced no query error. Existing Verify action becomes local Recheck settings with a cause/next action and retains draft; consumer recovery test passes.

findings.summary: Credential messages cross scope
findings.evidence: invalidate did not clear error/cliStatus on Project/connection changes. Ordinary messages now reset on actual scope changes while scoped retained-effect notices and same-scope Cancel drafts survive.

findings.summary: Failure fixtures do not match wire enums
findings.evidence: Unsupported credentials/repository failure-kind strings were present and are corrected; fabricated responses now parse shared schemas. The separate claim that the success fixture lacked capabilities.read is disproved by its existing read:true field.

findings.summary: Late Connect commits or stored-file effects are hidden
findings.evidence: Same verified early-return defect as blind-1. Fresh authoritative recovery and scope-retained notices repair both successful commits and partial credential effects; no stale response is directly adopted after Restore.

findings.summary: CLI changes during final status probe
findings.evidence: Same verified post-fingerprint await as blind-4. Final operational capture/comparison refuses changed account/source and selected metadata follows that capture.

findings.summary: Embedded login reading
findings.evidence: Accepted D4 in the named story preparation and original Epic7 acceptance explicitly select human-terminal gh auth login or pasted tokens; embedded/OAuth login is not an unresolved reading of that story.

findings.summary: Diff cannot prove workflow execution
findings.evidence: The diff alone cannot show execution history, but parent tool results establish exactly one renderer call, snapshot reads, mandatory implementation/four review agents and independent gates. Sprint hash remains unchanged and no tracking row was used as proof.

findings.summary: Running app entry point not exercised
findings.evidence: Final parent Safari fixture opened the actual built Connections route and dialog, performed Verify/Connect and observed actual header state. Native acceptance evidence supersedes the initial jsdom-only limitation.

findings.summary: Continuous browser to persistence journey missing
findings.evidence: Final native Safari fixture crossed real UI, HTTP, application, repository and disposable SQLite with controlled CLI/provider boundary, proved off/no rows before Connect and one read-only row/On after, then retained ID on reconnect/reload. Live account acceptance is separately deferred.

findings.summary: Header only inferred from query-cache assertions
findings.evidence: Actual SafetySwitchStrip is now mounted alongside the panel and its Off-to-On labels asserted. Parent native Safari additionally observed the real header after Connect and reload.

findings.summary: Real account and installed CLI acceptance remains unverified
findings.evidence: Transport interception and disposable CLI/provider fixture establish boundaries but not an actual account/repository authentication. If broken the impact is medium; a separately authorized presence-confirmed real GitHub/CLI smoke would settle it.

findings.summary: Complete native platform and reader matrix unperformed
findings.evidence: Parent Mac Safari observed heading focus, reverse-tab containment and keyboard opener return, but did not execute full VoiceOver/Windows/NVDA/Firefox release matrix. If native reader behavior is broken impact is medium; execute that bounded matrix to settle it.

findings.summary: Server does not receive a browser cancellation event
findings.evidence: An already submitted explicit Connect is authorized for its captured original Project. Client closing does not promise rollback/revocation. Proof binds submitted scope/epoch; late effects are now reconciled through fresh scoped reads and cannot enable another Project.

findings.summary: Ambiguous recovered connections selected arbitrarily
findings.evidence: New recovery initially used .find although same-name/target configurations are permitted. It now reuses only exactly one match; multiple matches keep creation blocked until explicit saved selection. Two-match consumer regression passes.

followup_risk: Native multiple-window lost-response/Restore recovery and actual CLI account transitions remain unverified beyond controlled consumer/server tests.
